card.name: Modal verb after a patient subject
card.fires_on: The helper word "should" (or "be" right after it, or "may") that follows a patient or drug subject and comes before the main verb in label instructions. A few hits are other words that sit before an expected continuation, like "at" or a plural ending.

modes.label: should after discontinuation
modes.description: "should" or "be" after a subject who stops a drug, leading into "be closely monitored".
modes.example: Patients who are coinfected with HIV-1 and HBV who discontinue EMTRIVA<< should>> be closely monitored with both clinical and laboratory

modes.label: should after overdose or therapy subject
modes.description: "should" after a patient or condition subject, leading into a management action.
modes.example: All patients suspected of tricyclic overdose<< should>> receive gastrointestinal decontamination.

modes.label: may be eligible
modes.description: "be" after "may" in a study recruitment sentence.
modes.example: If you are going to have surgery to treat a VS, you may<< be>> eligible to participate.

card.writes: The promoted tokens are mostly odd names and Chinese pieces, and the suppressed ones are r-endings, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It lights up on the word "should" or "may be" in label sentences that tell what patients need to have done.
